analysis: Examined NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift base/head: the only change (head 178-179) maps the new NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.Failure.bodyTooLarge to MediaIngest.MediaError.mediaTooLarge with a fixed, non-prompt-derived message. This preserves the file's rule that outward errors never serialize foreign descriptions (head 164-165). A MediaError passing through map again would hit head 212 and become invalidRequest, but this mapping is the terminal return, so no description leak results. The change alters status semantics (413 instead of 400) and does not change admission, cancellation, cacheScope plumbing (T-041), or the relay. The tests (head 16-26) now use NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes instead of the hardcoded 8 MiB. They assert the quote at the maximum, assert that maximum+1 yields bodyTooLarge, and assert that 0 bytes is invalidInput. Questions for integration: (1) The value of maximumEncodedBodyBytes and the encodedHeaderQuote implementation (NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.swift) are not in this batch. Integration should verify the bound was not raised beyond the earlier 8 MiB in a way that increases memory reservation. The quote is maximum*32 + 4 + 16 MiB, so a larger maximum scales reserved bytes, affecting availability under TB-007 and T-016-style resource exhaustion. (2) The HTTP status mapping for MediaError.mediaTooLarge is in MediaIngest/MLXOpenAIService. Integration should also confirm that the mapping does not echo the message unsafely and that bodyTooLarge is raised before any parsing or reservation. No regression was identified in the supplied evidence.
